originality.rationale: The literature covers the qualitative possibility of nonreal sketched Ritz eigenvalues and the standalone multivariate Student regression law. It does not in the inspected primary source material cover the curved-discriminant Gaussian probability and paired sharp square-root versus sketch-size-dependent polynomial asymptotics. A related deterministic three-state construction treats coordinate sketches and is logically incomparable to the random Gaussian event law. Bibliographic risks remain explicitly recorded.
residual_risks: Known Student-law formulas and literature on random two-by-two matrix discriminants might subsume the integral in a different notation; bounded searches and the primary-source inspection do not prove absolute uniqueness.
The Gaussian sketch is dense iid real Gaussian, whereas the motivating paper experiments mainly with sparse sign sketching; applicability to sparse sketches is unproved.
Finite numerical probability tests cannot certify all sketch sizes or the exact limiting constants; those follow from the analytical arguments.

value.rationale: Two-by-two real-Schur blocks signal a concrete algorithmic cost and spectral interpretation issue in symmetric eigensolvers using nonsymmetric Gaussian least-squares sketches. A sharp event law for a smallest interesting SPD coupled family gives exact base-rate rather than a possible/impossible classification. Universal sqrt-gap emergence versus s-dependent power tail precisely distinguishes what adding sketch rows can and cannot mitigate; unlike arbitrary parameters, gap and sketch rows are core numerical design variables.
